en: The Legend of the Elder Kiṅkaṇipupphiya From the Kaṇikārapupphiya Chapter of the Therāpadāna, Number Three.
“Resembling a priceless golden ornament,
the Omniscient Leader of the World,
having plunged into the burning water, [emerged].”
The Leader of the World was bathed.
Taking up a *kiṅkaṇī* flower,
I offered it to Vipassi.
With an uplifted mind and joyful heart,
[I honored] the Tādin, the Lord of Bipeds.
Ninety-one aeons ago,
The flower that I offered—
of this worship of the Buddha, I do not know a state of woe; this is its fruit.
In the twenty-seventh aeon,
there was a king named Bhīmaratha,
who was endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Kiṅkaṇipupphiya recited these verses.
This is the third legend (Apadāna) of the elder Kiṅkaṇipupphiya.
